items.name: Every skill directory contains a SKILL.md with a closed YAML frontmatter block
No invocation name is declared by more than one skill directory
items.notes: FIXED, then found insufficient. Renaming resolved the name: collision but MOVED it: all 3 pairs still had byte-identical description: and triggers:, which is what routing actually selects on. Pairs now carry distinct deprecation-pointer routing metadata. Criterion 8 added to measure that surface.

items.name: Every skill's name field equals its directory name
items.notes: FIXED, not waived. All 14 name: fields set to match their directories after the auditor rejected the waiver 0.0. Rename simulated first: 0 new collisions. NOTE: this did NOT free the pp-* namespace — skills/pp-hackernews/ and skills/pp-youtube/ still legitimately declare pp-hackernews and pp-youtube.

items.name: Every skill's routing is reachable: 40+ char description, or a '## When to invoke' section, or triggers:
items.notes: Criterion REWRITTEN. The original 40-char rule was wrong: gstack's catalog trim (T4) deliberately shortens Claude-host descriptions and moves routing to the body plus proactive-suggestions.json. All 39 description edits were REVERTED. Now passes honestly across 315 skills.

items.name: Every mirrored skill is byte-identical to its plugin copy
items.notes: fixed earlier this run; was 4 drifted

items.name: No generated Python bytecode is committed under skills/ or plugins/
items.notes: criterion rewritten after auditor rejected 46 false positives

items.name: RETIRED — 'shadows nothing in the repo tree' was unsatisfiable by construction
items.verified_by: n/a — retired, see contract third amendment
items.notes: The repo deliberately keeps one skill tree per harness, so every ported skill shadows itself by design. Replaced by criterion 9, which measures body drift rather than name presence.

items.name: No two skills share an identical description: or triggers:
items.notes: Rule rebuilt twice after audit. Now: similarity-based at 0.95 (exact equality fell to a trailing period), YAML-indentation triggers parser (the old one returned [] for every gstack skill), and it also hashes '## When to invoke'. Both evasions mutation-tested and failing correctly.

items.name: No skill's body differs across repo trees unless registered in cross-tree-variants.json with evidence
items.notes: 38 multi-tree names: 33 differ only in frontmatter (intentional per-harness porting), 5 in body. 3 registered as deliberate (impeccable, investor-competitive-dossier routers, openhands-niche-agency accuracy edit); 2 were genuinely stale and synced forward (ikigai -> .agents, skill-builder -> .claude). Mutation-tested both ways.
